title: Source-first mechanical ornithopter interpretation

aspect_ratio.reading: The rounded 'Say' span is 7.4 ft and the area paragraph states total area 6.61 ft² and AR=b²/S=8.29.
aspect_ratio.exclusion: The inconsistent 3.135 ft wing-length conversion is not used.

wrist_span_fraction.reading: The rounded wrist span is 3.7 ft, explicitly marked 50% of the 7.4 ft full span.

photographs.principle: Swan planform: broad constant-chord inner arm, rounded tapered outer hand wing; AR and wrist fraction are the source-derived dimensions.
photographs.unreadableOrUncertain: Some pencil annotations and the specimen/scaling provenance are faint; 3.135 ft conflicts with the other dimensions.
photographs.engineeringCompletion: The supplied 14 m span, four-segment outer ellipse and area normalization scale this proportion.

photographs.principle: Curved-plate section data are contextual rather than transferable full-scale coefficients.
photographs.unreadableOrUncertain: Axes, curve identities and Reynolds-number applicability are ambiguous.
photographs.engineeringCompletion: Separate supplied inner/outer polar tables are used and declared illustrative, not digitised from the chart.

photographs.principle: Compare candidate wing action with a desired sinusoidal trajectory and required vertical-force range; retain the human-carrying aim.
photographs.unreadableOrUncertain: No build dimensions or validated aircraft coefficients are supplied.
photographs.engineeringCompletion: The simulation computes forces causally rather than prescribing the target trajectory.

photographs.principle: Flapping creates cyclic lift and thrust and therefore small trajectory and airspeed variations; the text explicitly discusses a powered man-carrying ornithopter.
photographs.unreadableOrUncertain: Marginal handwriting is not treated as a settled specification.
photographs.engineeringCompletion: A 16 kW finite shaft-power model and supplied mass budget complete the powered aircraft.

photographs.principle: Longer working downstroke at low speed, equal periods at cruise, matching candidate lift/drag to required values, and resonant wing-wishbone-body dynamics.
photographs.unreadableOrUncertain: Crossed-out and marginal revisions are uncertain.
photographs.engineeringCompletion: A fixed timing-bias linkage and supplied spring, damping and distributed inertia implement these ideas.

photographs.principle: Resolve force from actual local hand-wing motion; use fore/aft movement, closing on recovery, elastic exchange and the resulting body pitching reaction.
photographs.unreadableOrUncertain: The prose gives no complete phase law or linkage dimensions.
photographs.engineeringCompletion: Explicit sine/cosine phase curves, two overlapping rigid leaves and coupled mass-matrix dynamics fill the gap.

photographs.principle: The continuation says recovery uses reduced area/span and local incidence changes; incidence, camber and thickness remain distinct.
photographs.unreadableOrUncertain: The later goshawk section percentages are examples, not swan specifications.
photographs.engineeringCompletion: Independent twist, camber and thickness metadata are used; supplied camber curves shape geometry and coefficients.

photographs.principle: Use a 5-6% inner arm section, thin curved/slotted hand wing, closing recovery, and conventional tail/rudder controls for the mechanical craft.
photographs.unreadableOrUncertain: Bird takeoff angles are descriptive and do not specify this aircraft.
photographs.engineeringCompletion: The model uses 5.5% inner and 0.8% outer thickness assumptions, sliding leaves, tailplane, elevator, fin, rudder and three wheels.

photographs.principle: Glide work is D times V and powered work additionally includes aerodynamic, trajectory and wing-inertia terms; elastic storage cannot be net propulsion.
photographs.unreadableOrUncertain: Missing appendices and tentative efficiency wording prevent a recovered quantitative design.
photographs.engineeringCompletion: Work counters integrate actual shaft, aerodynamic, transmission/damping and control work; the spring only exchanges stored energy.

massStatement.attribution: These, the engine, transmission and component allocations are supplied favourable engineering assumptions, not Stanley's figures.

limitations: Educational reduced model only: no structural validation, CFD, flexible-wing analysis or human-flight prediction.
The phase curves are a mechanical completion, not notebook samples.
Section pitching moment, overlap flow and unsteady wake/stall hysteresis are omitted.
The pilot, engine, wheels, coefficients and glide trim are engineering completions and are not claimed as Stanley's specification.
Missing appendices, source section data and revised equations remain missing.
